skeleton: tiny furry glider (Volaticotherium) sitting up on its back legs in three-quarter view facing left, little arms held out to the sides: root between the feet; body (pivot at the hips) with belly squash, the body piece carrying the cream throat up under the head (soft unoutlined top) and its bottom a soft cut the tail tucks behind; head with its round ears (soft unoutlined chin, no neck) on the throat, face carrying both eyes (the far one smaller, by the nose), brows, the pink nose, the whiskers on each side and the mouth; skinL/skinR — the cream gliding skin of each side, its own bone at the flank (behind the arms and legs), folding in towards the body (sx) when an arm comes in; armL (far) and armR (near) at the shoulders, behind the body; legL/legR at the hips, behind the body, in front of the skins; tail behind at its root; paws (both front paws held together) in front of the face for grooming; the body slot swaps to a spread glide sail (head on top) in flight and to a curled-up sleeping ball.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a tiny, fluffy gliding mammal, like a little flying squirrel: soft grey-blue fur with a cream tummy, sitting up on its back legs with its little arms held out to the sides, the cream gliding skin stretched between its front paws and back feet on each side like a small cape, a long thin tail, turned to the left. Draw this exact little glider as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, fur texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body with its throat: the small upright body with its soft cream tummy and grey-blue furry sides, turned as in image 1, WITHOUT head, without arms, without legs, without tail and WITHOUT the gliding skin: the grey-blue fur of each side ends in the drawing's dark outline along the side. At the top, the cream throat goes straight up, as wide as it is under the chin in image 1, and ends in a soft, smooth edge with NO outline (it is hidden under the head). At the bottom, between where the legs join, the tummy is rounded with its outline; at the lower right, where the tail tucks behind, there is no stump and no bump.
2. the head with its two small round ears (pink inside), turned to the left as in image 1, with a completely blank face: no eyes, no eyebrows, no nose, no whiskers, no mouth line; keep the rosy cheeks and the grey-blue fur on top of the head; the cream face is one smooth shape. Keep its dark outline over the top of the head, round the ears and round the cheeks; under the chin its bottom edge is soft, with NO outline: the cream fur simply stops there.
3. the far arm (on the left of image 1): the short grey-blue furry arm reaching out to the left to its little pink paw with tiny round fingers, drawn whole from its shoulder (normally hidden behind the body) to the paw; its shoulder end, on the right, a smooth rounded edge with no outline across it.
4. the near arm (on the right of image 1): the short grey-blue furry arm reaching out to the right to its little pink paw with tiny round fingers, drawn whole from its shoulder (normally hidden behind the body) to the paw; its shoulder end, on the left, a smooth rounded edge with no outline across it.
5. the far gliding skin (on the left of image 1) alone: the soft cream, slightly see-through-looking membrane with faint thin lines, as in image 1, without the arm and without the leg: its top edge runs out to the left where the arm lies along it, its outer edge curves down from the wrist to the ankle with the drawing's dark outline, its bottom end narrows to the ankle; its inner edge on the right, where it joins the body's side, is a soft edge with NO outline (it tucks behind the body).
6. the near gliding skin (on the right of image 1) alone: the same cream membrane of the other side, without the arm and without the leg: its top edge runs out to the right where the arm lies along it, its outer edge curves down from the wrist to the ankle with the drawing's dark outline, its bottom end narrows to the ankle; its inner edge on the left, where it joins the body's side, is a soft edge with NO outline.
7. the far back leg (on the left of image 1): the grey-blue furry thigh and little pink foot with soft round toes, drawn whole from the top of the thigh (normally hidden behind the body); its top a smooth rounded end with no outline across it.
8. the near back leg (on the right of image 1): the grey-blue furry thigh and little pink foot with soft round toes, drawn whole from the top of the thigh (normally hidden behind the body); its top a smooth rounded end with no outline across it.
9. the long thin tail with short grey-blue fur, curving as in image 1, drawn whole from its thin base (normally hidden behind the body) to the rounded tip; its base a smooth rounded end with no outline across it.
10. the little glider gliding through the air, WITHOUT its head and WITHOUT its tail, seen a little from below and from the side, flying to the left: its grey-blue furry body stretched out flat, the cream tummy showing, both front paws reaching out forward and to the sides, both back feet stretched out behind, and the cream gliding skin pulled out wide and flat between each front paw and back foot like a small square kite or sail, its outer edges gently curved with the dark outline. At its front, on the upper left, where the head would sit, a soft rounded neck end with NO outline across it (hidden under the head); at its back, on the right, a soft edge with no outline where the tail would join.
11. the little glider curled up into a round, fluffy ball, fast asleep: its grey-blue furry back rounded over, its long thin tail wrapped round the front of the ball, its little head tucked down in front showing its round ears, pink nose and both eyes peacefully closed (curved sleeping lines), the cream gliding skin folded snugly round it like a blanket, its little paws tucked in.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. Nothing sharp: no teeth, no claws. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a tiny, fluffy gliding mammal like a little flying squirrel; image 2 shows the same little glider cut into puppet parts, with a blank face (no eyes, nose, whiskers or mouth). Draw the glider's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the glider in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2. Its head is turned to the left: its far eye (on the left of image 1, beside the nose) is a little smaller and narrower than its near eye (on the right of image 1). In image 1 both eyes look up and to the left: each big shiny dark-brown iris sits towards the upper left of its eye, with a white sparkle.

Draw each piece on its own, upright, in five tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
Row 1, the far eye (the smaller eye, on the LEFT of image 1), six times:
1. as it is in image 1: a big shiny dark-brown iris with a white sparkle, looking up and to the left.
2. wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, with its white sparkle, looking the same way.
3. closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc, like an upside-down U, with a few small lashes.
4. sad: open, the dark-brown iris with a white sparkle looking down and to the left, a thin shine of a welling tear along its bottom rim; no lid slanting across it.
5. crying: squeezed shut, a soft lid line as wide as the open eye, curving down at both ends like a little frown (a sad closed eye, not a smile), and one small light-blue teardrop just below it.
6. gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line as wide as the open eye, with a few short lashes.
Row 2, the near eye (the bigger eye, on the RIGHT of image 1), the same six in the same order; open, it looks the same way as row 1, up and to the left, the iris towards the upper left of the eye.
Row 3: 13. the far eyebrow (over the left eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 14. the same far eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (right) end. 15. the near eyebrow (over the right eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 16. the same near eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (left) end. 17. the little pink nose as in image 1, a soft rounded triangle with a tiny shine. 18. the far whiskers (on the left of image 1): three thin dark-brown whiskers fanning out to the left, their right ends meeting at one point. 19. the near whiskers (on the right of image 1): three thin dark-brown whiskers fanning out to the right, their left ends meeting at one point.
Row 4, the small mouth under the nose, none with any teeth: 20. the mouth as it is in image 1: a small closed smile, a little curved line curling up at the corners. 21. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, rounded, the inside smooth and pink with a little pink tongue, no teeth. 22. the mouth open in a small round 'o', smooth and pink inside. 23. the mouth in a small sad frown. 24. the mouth open in a big round yawn, smooth and pink inside with a little tongue, no teeth.
Row 5: 25. both little pink front paws held up together, palms towards the face, their tiny round fingers curled, each with a short bit of grey-blue furry wrist below it, as when the glider washes its face; the wrists' bottom ends soft with no outline across them.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the glider spreads its arms and legs wide and glides down and across to the left on its stretched gliding skin, swaying gently, then tips up, lands on its feet and folds its skin.
the glider scurries along to the left on its little back legs, leaning forward with its gliding skin folded in and its long tail trailing, then sits up.
the glider crouches, jumps up high for joy with its arms and gliding skin stretched out, and lands with a little squash.
the glider shakes its head no, its whiskers swishing.
the glider looks one way, then the other, then back.

pause.shows: the glider looking off to the side, curious

animations.description: the glider laughs and laughs, bouncing with giggles.
the glider does a happy little dance, swaying from side to side and lifting one little arm, then the other, its tail swishing.
the glider talks, its mouth moving, its head bobbing a little.
the glider cries, head down, its little shoulders shaking with sobs.

pause.shows: the glider crying, head down, eyes squeezed shut with tears

animations.description: the glider gives a big yawn, closes its eyes and dozes off sitting up, its arms folded in, then wakes up, blinks and smiles.

pause.shows: the glider dozing sitting up, eyes shut, head drooped

animations.description: the glider lifts one little paw high and waves hello.
the glider shivers and trembles, cold or scared, its gliding skin pulled in tight.
the glider stretches its little arms out wide and stands up tall, showing off its gliding skin like a cape, holds it there, then folds it back in.

pause.shows: the glider standing tall with its arms stretched out wide, its gliding skin spread like a cape

animations.description: the glider lifts both little paws to its face and washes it, rub-rub-rub round its nose and whiskers, then smooths itself down and smiles, all clean.

pause.shows: the glider washing its face with both little paws, eyes shut

animations.description: the glider lifts its little pink nose and sniffs the air, its whiskers twitching, sniff-sniff.
the glider tucks in its head, wraps its long tail round and curls up into a round fluffy ball, fast asleep, then uncurls, stretches and smiles.

pause.shows: the glider curled up into a round fluffy ball, fast asleep

animations.description: the glider ducks down small, then slowly lifts its head and peeks out with big round eyes, looks this way and that, and pops up happily.

pause.shows: the glider crouched low, peeking out with big round eyes
